name: round_number_reversal_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Round numbers (multiples of 50 or 100 for NIFTY, multiples of 10/50/100 for stocks) act as psychological support/resistance because traders cluster limit orders and stops at these levels. When price approaches a round number with declining momentum, the order cluster absorbs the move and reverses it. The inefficiency exists due to anchoring bias — humans fixate on round numbers for order placement. Not fully arbitraged because the reversal is probabilistic (60-65% success) and each instance is small edge.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 stocks priced > ₹500 (round numbers more impactful at higher prices)

indicators.name: nearest_round
indicators.purpose: nearest round number (50 or 100 depending on stock price)

long.confirmation: first green bar within 0.15% of round number

short.confirmation: first red bar within 0.15% of round number

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% beyond the round number (if round is support, stop 0.2% below)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes 0.2% beyond the round number (level broken)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer reversals aligned with VWAP direction
other_filters: only trade at 'major' rounds (100s for stocks >1000, 50s for 500-1000)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — behavioral, anchoring bias is persistent

weaknesses: When a round number breaks with volume, the reversal bet fails hard. Stop-hunting at round numbers is also common — market makers exploit this.
Thin per-trade edge (20 bps). High sensitivity to cost assumptions.
Definition of 'round number' is arbitrary — should you use 50s, 100s, 500s? The choice affects signal frequency and quality in hard-to-predict ways.
prior_art: Round number / psychological level trading. Widely discussed. See: behavioral finance literature on anchoring (Kahneman & Tversky).
notes: Track hit rate by round number 'size' (50 vs 100 vs 500). Larger rounds should have higher hit rate.
